title: VF arrest, ROSC and STEMI
stem: A 58-year-old man complaining of chest pain collapses in the ED waiting area in front of the triage nurse. He has been brought into Resus 1 on a trolley. He is unresponsive. You lead the arrest team.

phases.title: Arrest
phases.goal: Confirm it, call for help and the defibrillator, start high-quality CPR, give roles.

phases.title: Shock
phases.goal: Pads on during CPR; VF: shock, then straight back to CPR.

phases.title: CPR loop
phases.goal: Shocks at the 2-minute checks; adrenaline after the 2nd shock, amiodarone after the 3rd; airway and capnography; Hs and Ts.

phases.title: Post-cardiac arrest care
phases.goal: Secure the airway, ventilate for normocapnia, hit the targets.

phases.title: The cause
phases.goal: 12-lead ECG and V4R; primary PCI; antiplatelet and heparin; no nitrates.

review.text: Algorithm. This station follows AHA ACLS, as Hong Kong ACLS courses do and as your notes do: adrenaline after the 2nd shock, amiodarone after the 3rd; post-ROSC SpO2 92–98%, MAP at least 65, temperature 32–37.5 °C for 24 hours. RCUK/ERC give adrenaline after the 3rd shock and aim for SpO2 94–98%. Say which you follow if asked.
AHA 2025 and RCUK/ERC 2025 details are quoted from memory; I could not check the documents here. The scored points are the same in the 2020 and 2023 versions.

notes:
Checked against Resuscitation Council UK 2025 adult ALS and post-resuscitation care guidelines (ERC 2025, ILCOR 2025), ESC 2023 ACS guidelines, and AHA 2025.

Shockable rhythm: shock as soon as possible (biphasic at least 150 J for the first shock; escalate if the device allows), resume CPR immediately for 2 minutes without a pulse check. Adrenaline 1 mg and amiodarone 300 mg after the third shock; adrenaline every 3–5 minutes (alternate loops); amiodarone 150 mg after the fifth shock (lidocaine 100 mg if amiodarone is not available). Place the apical pad directly below the armpit in the mid-axillary line; after three failed shocks consider a vector change to antero-posterior. RCUK 2025 does not recommend routine double sequential defibrillation.

Airway: basic airway or supraglottic airway is acceptable; intubate only if skilled (over 95% success within two attempts, pause under 5 s). Waveform capnography for every advanced airway.

Post-ROSC (RCUK/ERC–ESICM 2025): SpO2 94–98%, PaCO2 4.7–6.0 kPa, systolic over 100 or MAP 60–65 mmHg, actively prevent fever (37.5 °C or less) for 36–72 hours in comatose patients, treat seizures (levetiracetam or valproate), prognosticate at 72 hours or later. ST elevation after ROSC → emergency angiography and primary PCI.

Inferior STEMI: check right-sided leads (V4R) for right ventricular infarction; avoid nitrates and keep preload.

Your notes point to the AHA 2025 ACLS algorithm and highlights; the RCUK/ERC sequence here matches it on the scored points (AHA also gives adrenaline after the second shock in some teaching; RCUK after the third).

Perfect script (AHA ACLS, as taught in Hong Kong) checked against four mark schemes: an AHA megacode checklist, an RCUK ALS checklist, an HKCEM-style resuscitation scheme and a keyword scheme. Added from that check: roles and closed-loop at the start, charging during compressions, the Hs and Ts named in full, ETCO2 for CPR quality, V4R and the nitrate warning said aloud, ICU after PCI, heparin.

steps.label: Arrest
steps.hint: Confirm the arrest in 10 seconds; help and the defibrillator; high-quality CPR; roles.

opts.t: Mr Choi, can you hear me? Unresponsive, not breathing normally, no carotid pulse in 10 seconds: this is a cardiac arrest.
Call the arrest team and bring the defibrillator, please.
opts.mark: Calls for help and the defibrillator

opts.t: Start high-quality CPR: 30 to 2, 5 to 6 cm deep, 100 to 120 a minute, full recoil, minimal interruptions.
I'll lead. Nurse Tam, pads on while compressions continue; bag-valve-mask with high-flow oxygen. Closed-loop, please.
opts.mark: Leads: allocates pads and airway; closed-loop communication

steps.label: Defibrillator
steps.hint: Pads on during CPR; VF: unsynchronised, 150 J or more; all clear.

opts.t: Pads on and shock
opts.performHint: CPR continues while you place the pads. VF: SYNC off, 150 J or more, CHARGE, ALL CLEAR, SHOCK.
mark: Correct pad placement without stopping CPR
All clear, oxygen away before the shock

steps.label: Team
steps.hint: Straight back on the chest; shocks at each 2-minute rhythm check, charging during compressions.

opts.t: Shock delivered: resume CPR immediately for 2 minutes, no pulse check.
opts.mark: Resumes CPR immediately after the shock

opts.t: Rhythm check at 2 minutes: still VF. Charge during compressions, all clear, second shock, then straight back to CPR.
opts.mark: Second shock at the 2-minute check, charging during compressions

opts.t: Rhythm check: still VF. Third shock, CPR straight on.
opts.mark: Third shock at the next check

opts.t: Supraglottic airway with waveform capnography; ventilate 10 a minute with continuous compressions

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: Adrenaline 1 mg after the second shock, then every 3 to 5 minutes; amiodarone 300 mg after the third.

opts.t: Adrenaline 1 mg in 10 mL (1:10,000) 1 mg IV, then every 3–5 minutes
opts.mark: Adrenaline 1 mg after the second shock, then every 3–5 minutes

opts.t: Amiodarone 300 mg IV
opts.mark: Amiodarone 300 mg after the third shock

steps.label: Rhythm check
steps.hint: After the drugs and the next cycle: rhythm, pulse, ETCO2.

opts.t: Organised rhythm at the check: carotid pulse present, and the ETCO2 has jumped. We have ROSC.
opts.r: Sinus rhythm at 96 with a pulse. ETCO2 rose sharply before the check.
opts.early: Keep going: CPR, shocks at the checks, the drugs.

steps.label: During CPR
steps.hint: Hs and Ts aloud; access and a gas; swap compressors; ETCO2 for CPR quality.

opts.t: Reversible causes, Hs and Ts: hypoxia, hypovolaemia, hydrogen ion, hypo- or hyperkalaemia, hypothermia; tension pneumothorax, tamponade, toxins, thrombosis. Chest pain first: coronary thrombosis is most likely.
opts.mark: Considers the Hs and Ts; names coronary thrombosis

opts.t: IV access, and a blood gas with potassium, please.
opts.mark: Access and a gas during CPR
opts.r: Nurse Tam: Gas: K 4.1, pH 7.18, lactate 6.

opts.t: Swap compressors every 2 minutes; ETCO2 below 10 means we need better compressions.
opts.mark: Rotates compressors; uses ETCO2 to monitor CPR quality

steps.label: Intubate
steps.hint: GCS 3 after ROSC: secure the airway.

Airway.t: Intubate: laryngoscope, tube through the cords, cuff up, capnography
Airway.early: Not in the middle of CPR.

steps.label: Ventilator
steps.hint: Set it yourself: normocapnia after ROSC.

opts.t: Set the ventilator
opts.performHint: 80 kg, GCS 3 after ROSC. A controlled mode, 6–8 mL/kg, a normal rate for PaCO2 4.7–6.0 kPa. START.
mark: Oxygen, PEEP and a pressure limit

steps.label: After ROSC
steps.hint: Post-cardiac arrest care: oxygen, pressure, temperature, glucose.

opts.t: Post-cardiac arrest care: titrate oxygen to SpO2 92 to 98%.
Blood pressure: systolic at least 90, MAP at least 65; fluids, then noradrenaline if needed.
opts.mark: Blood pressure target: MAP at least 65

opts.t: Targeted temperature management: 32 to 37.5 °C for at least 24 hours, and prevent fever.
Check his glucose, put in an arterial line, and repeat the gas.

steps.label: Investigations
steps.hint: 12-lead ECG now; right-sided leads for an inferior STEMI; chest film for the tube.

ECG.r: ST elevation in II, III and aVF (III more than II) with reciprocal depression in I and aVL. "Inferior STEMI."
ECG.mark: Identifies inferior STEMI with reciprocal change

ECG.r: 1 mm ST elevation in V4R. "Right ventricular infarction."

steps.label: Phone
steps.hint: Emergency primary PCI; no nitrates with RV infarction; ICU after.

opts.t: Cardiology: VF arrest, ROSC after three shocks, an inferior STEMI with right ventricular infarction. He needs emergency primary PCI.
opts.r: Cardiologist: Cath lab in 15 minutes. Give aspirin and heparin.

opts.t: Right ventricular infarction: no nitrates, and keep him well filled.
And an ICU bed for after the cath lab.

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: Aspirin loading; heparin for the cath lab.

opts.t: Aspirin 300 mg (NG or PR)
Unfractionated heparin 70–100 units/kg IV bolus

qs.q: When is amiodarone first given in VF?
qs.a: 300 mg after the 3rd shock; 150 mg as the second dose
wrong: 150 mg after the 3rd shock; 300 mg as the second dose
300 mg after every shock up to a total of 900 mg
Only after ROSC, as a 24-hour infusion

qs.q: First-shock energy on a biphasic defibrillator (AHA)?
qs.a: 120–200 J as the maker advises, or the maximum
wrong: 50 J, then increase by 50 J each time

qs.a: 32–37.5 °C for at least 24 hours, then prevent fever
wrong: Allow up to 39 °C to support immunity

qs.q: What to consider after three failed shocks?
wrong: Stop resuscitation, as VF after three shocks is futile
Double the adrenaline dose to 2 mg
Give atropine 3 mg as a single dose

badge.name: Shock and Awe
badge.flavor: Shock early, CPR straight after. Three shocks, then the drugs.

cards.q: AHA ACLS: in VF, the first adrenaline is given…
cards.why: Then every 3–5 minutes. RCUK/ERC give it after the third shock.

cards.q: Lidocaine dose in VF if amiodarone is unavailable?
options: 100 mg, then 50 mg after the fifth shock
300 mg, then 150 mg after the fifth shock

cards.q: Where should the apical defibrillator pad sit?
options: Over the left nipple, on the breast
Over the lower sternum, left of midline
On the left shoulder, below the clavicle
cards.why: 2025 guidance stresses correct lateral pad placement.

options: Systolic at least 90, MAP at least 65
Systolic above 160 mmHg to perfuse the brain
MAP above 90 mmHg in every patient

cards.q: ECG after ROSC shows ST elevation. Next?
options: Wait 72 hours for neuroprognostication, then decide
CT head first in every case
cards.why: STEMI after ROSC goes to the cath lab.

cards.q: Which lead best shows right ventricular infarction?

script.say: Mr Choi, can you hear me? Unresponsive, not breathing normally, no carotid pulse in 10 seconds: this is a cardiac arrest. Call the arrest team and bring the defibrillator.

Start high-quality CPR: 30 to 2, 5 to 6 cm deep, 100 to 120 a minute, full recoil, minimal interruptions. I'll lead. Nurse Tam, pads on while compressions continue; bag-valve-mask with high-flow oxygen. Closed-loop, please.
Pause for a rhythm check: VF, a shockable rhythm. Continue compressions while I charge to 200 joules, unsynchronised. Oxygen away, all clear: shocking.
script.do: Pads below the right clavicle and in the left mid-axillary line; SYNC off; charge during compressions; all clear; shock.

script.say: Shock delivered: resume CPR immediately for 2 minutes, no pulse check.

Reversible causes, Hs and Ts: hypoxia, hypovolaemia, hydrogen ion, hypo- or hyperkalaemia, hypothermia; tension pneumothorax, tamponade, toxins, thrombosis. He had chest pain: coronary thrombosis is most likely.
IV access and a blood gas with potassium, please. Supraglottic airway with waveform capnography; ventilate 10 a minute with continuous compressions.
Rhythm check at 2 minutes: still VF. Charge during compressions, all clear, second shock, then straight back to CPR. Adrenaline 1 mg IV now, then every 3 to 5 minutes.
Swap compressors every 2 minutes. ETCO2 below 10 means we need better compressions.
Rhythm check: still VF. Third shock, CPR straight on. Amiodarone 300 mg IV.
Organised rhythm at the check: carotid pulse present, and the ETCO2 has jumped. We have ROSC.
He's GCS 3: I'll secure the airway with an endotracheal tube and waveform capnography, and set the ventilator for normocapnia: a controlled mode, 6 to 8 mL per kg, PaCO2 35 to 45.
script.do: Intubate; ventilator: controlled mode, 6–8 mL/kg, rate for normocapnia, oxygen and PEEP.

script.say: Post-cardiac arrest care: oxygen titrated to SpO2 92 to 98%; systolic at least 90 and MAP at least 65, fluids then noradrenaline if needed; targeted temperature management at 32 to 37.5 °C for at least 24 hours, and prevent fever; glucose, an arterial line and a repeat gas.

script.do: ST elevation in II, III and aVF with reciprocal change in I and aVL: inferior STEMI. V4R: 1 mm ST elevation: right ventricular infarction.

script.say: Cardiology: VF arrest, ROSC after three shocks, an inferior STEMI with right ventricular infarction. He needs emergency primary PCI. Right ventricular infarction: no nitrates, keep him well filled. And an ICU bed for after the cath lab.
Aspirin 300 mg via NG or PR, and heparin for the cath lab.
